{{Short description|Palindromic prime number}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2025}} 
[[File:Belphegor's prime.svg|thumb|Symbol of Belphegor's prime, represented by the Greek letter π upside down]]

'''Belphegor's prime''' is the [[palindromic prime]] number '''{{val|1000000000000066600000000000001}}''' (10<sup>30</sup> + 666 × 10<sup>14</sup> + 1), a number which reads the same both backwards and forwards and is only divisible by itself and one.

In the [[short scale]], this number would be named "one nonillion, sixty-six quadrillion, six hundred trillion one." In the [[long scale]], this number's name would be "one quintillion, sixty-six billiard, six hundred billion one."

== History ==
Belphegor's prime was first discovered by [[Harvey Dubner]],<ref name="ao"/> a mathematician known for his discoveries of many large prime numbers and prime number forms. For Belphegor's prime in particular, he discovered the prime while determining a sequence of primes it belongs to.

The name "Belphegor's prime" was coined by author [[Clifford A. Pickover]] in 2012.<ref name="Pickover2012">{{cite web|last=Pickover|first=Clifford A.|author-link=Clifford A. Pickover|date=2012|title=Belphegor's Prime: 1000000000000066600000000000001|url=https://sprott.physics.wisc.edu/pickover/pc/1000000000000066600000000000001.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250715032202/https://sprott.physics.wisc.edu/pickover/pc/1000000000000066600000000000001.html|archive-date=2025-07-15|access-date=2016-09-17}}</ref> [[Belphegor]] is one of the [[Seven Princes of Hell]]; specifically, "the demon of inventiveness".<ref name="Pickover2012"/> The number itself contains [[superstitious]] elements that have given it its name: the number [[666 (number)|666]] at the heart of Belphegor's prime is widely associated as being the [[number of the beast]], used in symbolism to represent one of the creatures in the [[apocalypse]] or, more commonly, the devil. This number is surrounded on either side by thirteen zeroes and is 31 digits in length (thirteen reversed), with [[13 (number)|thirteen]] itself long [[Triskaidekaphobia|regarded superstitiously as an unlucky number]] in Western culture.

== Mathematics ==
A ''Belphegor number'' is a palindromic number in the form of <math>1(0...)666(0...)1</math>. The sequence of the first four Belphegor numbers is:

<math display=block>16661, 1066601, 100666001, 10006660001, \ldots</math>

Dubner noticed that 16661 is a prime number. By adding zeroes directly on both sides of the 666, while making it always start and end with a 1, Dubner found more palindromic prime numbers, including the Belphegor prime, which is second in the sequence. This sequence eventually became the ''Belphegor primes'', named after the number.<ref name="ao"/> The equal number of zeroes on each side of 666 in the first few Belphegor primes is:<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A232448|Indices of Belphegor primes: numbers k such that the decimal number 1 0...0(k 0's) 666 0...0(k 0's) 1 (i.e., A232449(k)) is prime.|access-date=2024-10-09}} {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20250715232450/https://oeis.org/A232448|title=Archived}} from the original on 15 July 2025.</ref><ref name="ao"/>

<math display=block>0, 13, 42, 506, 608, 2472, 2623, 28291, 181298, \ldots</math>

Belphegor's prime contains 13 zeroes on either side of the central 666, and thus corresponds to the second number in this sequence.
